subject: Pilot concession: credit-bucket alternative to 2-week time extension
messages:
From: Ava Li <ava.li@brightharbor.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightharbor.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: request to convert unused days to credit bucket

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the run-through earlier this week. Our engineers burned through the initial pilot window faster than expected while testing the streaming/high-concurrency paths. We have ~7 unused pilot days left in the current timebox but several teams still need to hit their integration milestones.

Before we ask for a full time extension, procurement asked whether you can convert unused days into a credit bucket we can draw against for extra runtime during the next 4 weeks. Ideally: a flexible credit bucket (hours or token-based) that BrightHarbor can use across teams and a short addendum to the SOW instead of another full amendment.

Attached is a brief usage export showing the burst last Wednesday. Can you confirm if Redwood would:
- convert N unused days into an equivalent credit bucket, and
- what the pricing/discount for that conversion would look like (any minimums or caps)?

If not possible, we may take the 2-week extension route, but procurement prefers a credit approach for flexibility.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

— Ava
Ava Li
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightHarbor
attachments: pilot-usage-report.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: request to convert unused days to credit bucket

Hi Ava —

Appreciate the context and the export; that spike is helpful. We can take two pragmatic approaches here:

Option A — 2-week time extension (no charge):
- We extend the pilot by 14 calendar days on the existing timebox and keep the same sequencing for the SLA and telemetry.
- Good if you need uninterrupted calendar time to finish validation across teams.

Option B — Convert unused days to a credit bucket (recommended by procurement):
- We can convert the 7 unused days into a token-hour credit bucket redeemable over 30 days.
- Standard conversion math: 1 pilot day = X token-hours (see attached conversion worksheet in POC_CreditSwap_v2.pdf).
- For a credit conversion, we typically apply a concession discount; internally I need approval for anything >15% off list. My ask: would BrightHarbor consider a short pre-payment for the bucket (to cover commit) or do you need the bucket as a pure creditized addendum?

I'll loop Marissa for quick approval guidance on the discount range so we can give procurement a firm number. If you prefer, we can also do a hybrid: 1-week free extension + convert the remaining 3 days to a smaller credit bucket.

Quick timeline: if you give the go-ahead today I can get a short term-sheet over by Monday and we can turn that into a 48-hour signature/DocuSign process.

Onwards —
Jonas
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot: request to convert unused days to credit bucket

Jonas / David —

Thanks for the heads-up. Approvals framework below — keep it tight and make the offer clear to the customer:

- Discount: approve up to 15% off list when converting unused pilot days into a short-term credit bucket (30-day redemption window). Anything >15% needs VP approval.
- Max concession cap without finance signoff: $3,000 USD equivalent (we can internalize smaller currency conversions).
- Hybrid: approve 1-week free extension plus convert remaining days at up to 10% if customer prefers to avoid prepay.
- Contract path: retail with a 1-page addendum (no whole SOW rewrite). Use pilot-concessions-termsheet.docx as the template — include conversion math and redemption rules.

Jonas: please give the customer the 15%/3k option as the baseline. If they push for more, escalate to me with the business case (expansion ARR, strategic logo, reference OK).

David: cover the billing language (prepay vs invoice after redemption) and add the short clause on data retention during the extended window.

— Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
attachments: pilot-concessions-termsheet.docx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Li <ava.li@brightharbor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@brightharbor.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: 7-day conversion to 30-day credit bucket (BrightHarbor)

Hi Ava —

Following internal review, here's a proposed, short-path option that keeps procurement flexibility and avoids a full timebox amendment. This is what we can sign and turn around quickly:

Proposal (final):
- Convert 7 unused pilot days into an equivalent token-hour credit bucket redeemable over 30 days.
- Discount: 15% off list for the converted bucket (approved).
- Concession cap: total value not to exceed $3,000 USD under this exchange.
- Billing: Redwood issues invoice upon signature for the net amount (prepay). Credits are consumed and reconciled on monthly usage statements; unused credits expire at 30 days.
- Addendum: 1-page addendum attached (POC_CreditSwap_v2.pdf) — no SOW rewrite.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I'll attach the one-page addendum (DocuSign) and we can sign this week.
2) David will confirm the billing flow and send a short invoice template if you choose prepay.
3) We can schedule a quick 20-min call to walk through the redemption rules and telemetry so your teams know how to draw credits.

DocuSign placeholder: https://www.docusign.com/exec/placeholder/BRH-DH8421

Ava — are you okay to proceed on the 15%/prepay path? If procurement needs non-prepay billing we can offer the hybrid (1-week extension + 10% for converted remainder) instead.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this so your teams can continue testing.

Best,
Jonas Weber
